title: Bootstrap Rust workspace, shared contracts and Windows/core CI
level: General Rust agent; contract review before dependent work
files: `rust/{Cargo.toml,Cargo.lock}`, the three crate manifests and minimal lib/main/model/error stubs, `.github/workflows/rust-ci.yml`, Rust contribution guide and `deny.toml`.
before: `requirements.txt`, `build.cmd`, `.github/workflows/Basic health check.yml` only compile Python; shared application state is in `elevenclock/globals.py`. Reference scat Cargo.toml, src/error.rs, src/lib.rs, rustfmt.toml and CI.
scope: Create `rust-rewrite` from current main with the reviewed planning documents included; keep legacy runtime/build intact. Feature PRs target this integration branch.

Create clock-core (platform-independent), clock-windows (Windows-only safe facade) and clock-app (Windows-only executable); edition 2024, MSRV 1.95.0, publish=false, locked dependencies. Forbid unsafe in core/app; all Win32 FFI stays in clock-windows.

Define only the shared models/errors/contracts in the dissection: PhysicalRect, TaskbarId/ShellGeneration, TaskbarSnapshot, ClockText, Cadence and app event/effect boundaries. Document ownership/units and do not implement later issues.

Adopt chrono, serde/serde_json, thiserror; app clap/anyhow/tracing; target-specific windows bindings. Add dependencies when first used. Match scat's targeted Clippy policy and release profile without importing its database/TUI stack.

Set up Linux core tests/doc tests; Windows MSRV workspace/all-target checks; Windows stable fmt, Clippy, tests/doc tests and locked x64 MSVC build. Audit failures must fail visibly; license policy must account for retained repository notices.
Document exact commands, branch policy and MSRV in one consistent contributor guide; configure cargo/action dependency updates for the rust/ location.
accept: Linux builds/tests clock-core without compiling Windows crates.
Windows MSRV and stable CI pass using --locked; formatting/Clippy enforcement is active.
API ownership/coordinate/time semantics are documented and enough to start R02, R04, R05 and R06 without circular dependencies.
No Python removal, workflow deletion or license rebranding.
validation: `cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --check`; Linux `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p clock-core --locked` and `--doc`; Windows `cargo check --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --locked`, `cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, workspace tests/doc tests and release build.
exclude: No Explorer probing, production formatter, GUI, installer or comprehensive new dependency stack.
handoff: CI URLs, the agreed public contracts, chosen crate feature flags and instructions for checking out the integration branch.

title: Probe native clock bounds and record a supported taskbar discovery strategy
level: Windows/COM specialist; interactive Windows desktop required
files: `clock-windows/src/taskbar/{mod,probe,uia,geometry}.rs`, a probe example, `docs/windows-evidence/discovery.md` and discovery ADR.
before: `elevenclock/__init__.py:572–774` finds Shell_TrayWnd/Shell_SecondaryTrayWnd and computes preferred geometry; there is no Rust clock-bounds contract yet.
scope: Enumerate taskbar HWNDs, map to monitors, record signed physical geometry, per-monitor DPI, OS build and shell generation.
Probe UI Automation and native child-window geometry for a clock-only rectangle. Use locale-independent properties; explicitly reject a rectangle that includes bell/Show Desktop/other tray controls.
Run UIA outside the UI thread with COM ownership on the worker, generation-tagged value results, a bounded/coalesced queue and observable failure reasons.

Measure call latency and stale-object behavior on Explorer restart. A deadline does not cancel COM: prove bounded teardown/cancellation or document an isolated same-executable helper alternative before downstream code depends on it. Never accumulate stalled workers.

Record candidate strategies, actual successful selectors and failure cases on two stock Windows 11 x64 builds, including a mixed-DPI second display. Publish exact build numbers, not a general Windows 11 claim.
Implement safe failure: return unsupported/no verified rectangle rather than guessing a slot or changing Explorer.
accept: Each accepted clock rect fits its taskbar/monitor and excludes adjacent control hit targets.
Probe stays responsive when UIA errors, stalls or returns stale data; generation mismatch is rejected.
Actual evidence supports a chosen discovery strategy and identifies untested/unsupported combinations.
Document a go/no-go result; leave the manual gate unchecked if no interactive desktop is available.
validation: Unit-test geometry validation with negative coordinates, invalid rectangles, DPI and generation mismatch; run the probe on recorded Windows builds and capture structured output plus annotated screenshots.
exclude: No overlay, renderer, guessed fixed offsets, localized label matching, Explorer injection or UIA objects sent across threads.
handoff: ADR, reproducible probe commands, verified selectors, output fixtures, exact Windows builds and an explicit COM timeout/teardown decision.

title: Prove a non-activating clock overlay and native calendar access
level: Windows shell specialist; interactive evidence is a hard gate
files: `clock-windows/src/overlay.rs`, prototype interaction adapter, `docs/windows-evidence/overlay-spike.md`; reuse R02 discovery.
before: `__init__.py:624–774` creates topmost Qt clocks/cover windows; `:799` defaults to Win+N. Rust needs evidence that an external overlay works without disabling Explorer's clock.
scope: Build a minimal overlay with test text `2642.2`, no settings UI. Use verified clock-only bounds, WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW/NOACTIVATE, borderless style and per-monitor DPI v2 manifest.
Cover native clock text with an opaque rectangle while leaving bell/Show Desktop targets intact. Prototype taskbar-relative z-order instead of unconditional global topmost.
Demonstrate auto-hide show/hide, foreground/fullscreen transitions, mixed DPI, Explorer restart and removal on discovery failure.
Test UIA invoke of the native clock; if unavailable test deliberate one-shot Win+N fallback. Do not recursively invoke the overlay or replay mouse clicks.
Record whether the native clock remains available after forced termination. If any mandatory condition fails, narrow support or amend design and keep P3 blocked.
accept: Screenshots/video and exact build IDs show complete clock coverage without adjacent control obstruction.
Overlay does not activate on display, appear in Alt-Tab or float over fullscreen/hidden taskbar.
Click opens native calendar/notifications on claimed builds; no repeated input/stuck modifiers.
Forced termination and unsupported discovery restore native access immediately; no persistent Explorer mutation.
Written P1 go/no-go references both R02 and R03 evidence.
validation: Run primary/all-display prototype on R02 builds, auto-hide both states, DPI change, open calendar, click neighbors, restart Explorer and kill the process. Unit-test any added z-order/visibility decisions where practical.
exclude: No finished settings, complete renderer, notification replication, shell patching or claimed universal Windows compatibility.
handoff: Prototype entry command, measured integration strategy and evidence table. P3 issues must not begin until this gate passes.

title: Implement validated datetime formatting and explicit ISO week-date presets
level: Suitable for a lower-level Rust agent; cross-platform pure logic
files: `clock-core/src/format.rs` and focused format tests/benchmark; do not modify shell or shared config implementation.
before: `__init__.py:988 loadTimeFormat`, `:1314 updateTextLoop`; `tools.py:153–190` uses Python strftime plus an arithmetic/time-offset DSL.
scope: Implement CompiledFormat::parse/render/cadence using owned tokens and chrono, consuming one DateTime<FixedOffset> snapshot.

Allow exactly the directives in the plan, Unicode literals, %% and one newline. Normalize CRLF; at most two nonempty lines, 256 input Unicode scalars and 512 rendered scalars; reject other controls, modifiers and unlisted directives with indexed errors.
Add ISO `%g%V.%u`, calendar-year `%y%V.%u`, and `%H:%M\n%g%V.%u` presets with explicit names. No expression/offset compatibility layer.
Classify seconds-containing formats as Second cadence; all others as Minute. Render once for all lines; English weekday/month names initially.
Provide preview helpers usable by settings and CLI without shell dependencies.
accept: Tests cover week 53, Monday/Sunday, leap day, literal percent, Unicode, malformed directives and all bounds.
Generated arbitrary input never panics or exceeds output bounds; errors use documented character spans.
No mutable global time, OS queries, HTML or arithmetic evaluation.
validation: Run core unit/doc tests, targeted proptest cases and a small Criterion parse-versus-render benchmark. Include explicit-offset Europe/Amsterdam DST snapshots without treating a fixed offset as a zone rule.
exclude: No Windows clock access, UI, config persistence, custom zones or legacy formatting DSL.
handoff: Token table, preset examples, test output and stable API for R05/R07/R10/R11.

title: Implement typed JSON configuration and reliable Windows replacement
level: Core work suitable for a lower-level agent; Windows persistence review required
before: `tools.py:205–278` stores booleans as file presence and strings in separate ~/.elevenclock files; writes can restart all clocks.
scope: Define schema v1 fields exactly as the dissection: schema_version, format, monitors(primary/all), font_size_pt(6–24), theme(system/light/dark). Reject unknown fields/versions and run R04 validation.
Implement missing-file defaults and malformed-file preservation with a visible load error plus defaults for the current launch. Do not overwrite broken input automatically.
Resolve Windows Known Folder LocalAppData/ElevenClockRust/config.json. Expose explicit-path store construction so CLI precedence stays in clock-app.
Implement same-directory temporary write, flush/close and tested Windows replacement for existing target and first create. Preserve active/disk state if saving fails; no remove-then-rename gap.
Return immutable ValidatedConfig only after successful validation; callers apply after successful persistence. Startup registration is not duplicated in JSON.
Provide explicit reload behavior; no watcher or legacy settings migration.
accept: Defaults round-trip; unknown fields/version, invalid enums, font bounds and malformed formats fail specifically.
Replacing an existing file works on Windows; failed writes/replacement leave prior bytes intact.
Corrupt input remains on disk and does not cause a rewrite loop or repeated destructive reset.
No changes to old ~/.elevenclock files.
validation: Core serde/validation tests; Windows temporary-directory tests for first write, replacement, locked/denied target and injected failure before replacement. Run on Windows, not only POSIX.
exclude: No settings controls, autostart toggling, per-monitor overrides, YAML/TOML or filesystem watcher.
handoff: Schema/example, load/save error behavior, Windows filesystem test evidence and store API.

title: Implement deterministic scheduling and per-taskbar visibility state
level: Suitable for a lower-level Rust agent; no interactive Windows needed
before: `__init__.py:1194–1338` polls visibility/text; `:179–283` rebuilds clocks; global screen/clock state is shared across callbacks.
scope: Implement next_delay and reduce(state,event)->effects against R01 contracts. Use passed wall snapshots and cadence, never live OS time in core.
Maintain Unavailable/Hidden(reason)/Visible per transient taskbar and shell generation; discard stale discovery. Reconcile additions/removals instead of recreating every clock.
Support topology/discovery, visibility/fullscreen, lock/unlock, theme/config, tick/time-change, ExplorerLost and Quit inputs.
Emit discovery, overlay create/destroy/bounds, hide/paint and timer effects; prevent duplicate windows and paint only on text/theme/geometry change.
Align second/minute cadence to next boundary; date-only rechecks each minute. Model resume/clock jumps as fresh time snapshots, not accumulated +24h offsets.
accept: Unknown bounds, stale generation, locked session, fullscreen or hidden taskbar never produce visible overlays.
ExplorerLost destroys/invalidate overlays; subsequent generation can recover without app restart.
Repeated identical events are idempotent; two monitors can have different visibility.
Tests cover backward/forward clock jumps, local midnight and fixed-offset DST transition inputs without sleeping.
validation: Core unit/property tests using fake time and event sequences; include monotonic wait versus wall snapshot distinction and negative-coordinate topology fixtures.
exclude: No WinEvent hooks, COM, actual timers, platform clock reads or framework/event-loop dependency.
handoff: State transition table, fixture sequences and precise effect contract for the runtime integrator.

title: Build DirectWrite clock rendering with DPI, theme and overflow handling
level: Windows graphics agent; P1 gate must be passed
files: `clock-windows/src/{render,theme,overlay}.rs`; replace prototype drawing while preserving proven R03 shell behavior.
before: Qt Label/stylesheet rendering, `checkAndUpdateBackground` at `__init__.py:1120` samples screen pixels; clock and cover widgets manage separate visual state.
scope: Render R04 ClockText via DirectWrite/Direct2D in the verified clock region with system font, configured point size and one/two-line layout.
Implement DPI conversion at explicit boundaries, preserving signed physical coordinates. UI thread owns graphics resources and HWNDs.
Use system/light/dark/high-contrast palettes with opaque coverage. Respect high-contrast over cosmetic theme choices; no screen capture.
Measure layout before painting/apply. If current/future text does not fit, report overflow and hide that monitor's overlay; never widen over bell/tray or silently truncate.
Cache text layouts/brushes appropriately, repaint only on dirty state and recover from device loss without leaked handles.
accept: Crisp readable text at 100/125/150/200% including mixed DPI; both supported line counts fit or yield explicit overflow.
No native text shows through; adjacent control targets remain unchanged.
Theme/high-contrast switch takes effect without restarting process.
Longer month/day/year-boundary output cannot overlap tray controls; device-loss path recreates resources.
validation: Pure layout boundary tests where possible plus interactive screenshots at the DPI/theme matrix, long-format and font-size tests, and a graphics resource recreation/handle-count check.
exclude: No animation, mica/transparency matching, screenshot sampling, icons for notifications or settings UI.
handoff: Renderer API, layout/overflow result types, DPI/theme screenshots and resource ownership notes.

title: Integrate event-driven runtime, multi-monitor reconciliation and Explorer recovery
level: Experienced Windows runtime agent; interactive desktop required
before: `__init__.py:245 screenCheckThread`, `:285` lockfiles, `:340` wake polling, `:977–979` per-clock threads and `:1943–1948` global workers.
scope: Wire core reducer effects to the proven discovery/renderer with one UI message loop and the R02 bounded UIA strategy.
Add per-user/session single-instance mutex and a fixed signal to show settings in an existing instance; duplicate launch must not add clocks.
Handle display/DPI/settings/theme/time, power/session and TaskbarCreated events plus filtered WinEvent hooks. Keep callbacks short; coalesce topology discovery.
Implement primary/all monitor modes with negative-coordinate/mixed-DPI topology, hotplug and primary swap; invalidate stale HWNDs and queued generation results.
Track actual taskbar auto-hide and fullscreen per monitor; supplement missing events with documented two-second recovery polling and bounded transition polling where needed.
Use one fresh local-time snapshot per update, monotonic waits and no high-frequency perpetual clock loop. On quit/failure unhook and release resources; leave native clock usable.
accept: Default two-line clock works on primary and all monitors without process restart for format/theme changes.
Explorer kill/restart restores tray/clock state and rejects old discovery results.
Hotplug, DPI changes, lock/unlock, resume and timezone/manual time changes reconcile correctly.
Second launch signals the existing process; no lockfiles, unbounded threads or leaked hooks.
Unsupported geometry/overflow removes only affected overlays and surfaces a reason.
validation: Reducer regression tests plus recorded interactive matrix for shell restart, monitor changes, auto-hide/fullscreen, sleep/lock and clock changes; capture steady-state thread/handle counts.
exclude: No ad hoc second state machine, WNF, internet sync, global keyboard hook or permanent Explorer modification.
handoff: Event-to-core mapping, fallback polling rates, shutdown semantics and actual Windows run evidence.

title: Finish clock actions, tray controls and accessible native interaction
level: Windows UI/accessibility agent; interactive validation required
files: `clock-windows/src/{interaction,tray}.rs`, minimal overlay accessibility provider and settings-open callback wiring.
before: `__init__.py:1340–1407,1850` custom gestures/keyboard shortcuts; `tools.py:409 TaskbarIconTray` and notification labels overlap the clock UI.
scope: Productionize the R03 selected native calendar invocation/fallback, with one activation per click and cleanup on failure.
Add fixed right-click/tray menu: Settings, Reload settings, Pause/Resume replacement and Exit. Keyboard activation opens the same menu.
Re-register tray icon on Explorer restart using the runtime's existing recovery event; do not build a second recovery loop.
Expose the displayed clock through a minimal UIA name/value and invoke action. Avoid second-by-second screen-reader announcements.
Keep overlay non-activating; settings/menu may take focus intentionally. Unknown invocation failure removes overlay for native access and records the reason.
accept: Mouse and keyboard users can reach Settings/Exit; paused mode reliably shows the native clock.
Calendar opens once without stuck modifiers or recursive overlay invocation.
Bell/Show Desktop and normal app focus remain usable.
Screen reader can identify and invoke clock; no live announcement flood.
validation: Interactive mouse/keyboard and Narrator tests on supported builds; invocation-failure and Explorer restart tests; unit-test action dispatch/coalescing where appropriate.
exclude: No arbitrary commands, customizable double/middle gestures, duplicated notification counter, shell injection or synthetic mouse relay.
handoff: Action behavior table, UIA pattern choice, manual accessibility results and callbacks for R10.

title: Add compact native settings with live date-format preview
level: Windows controls agent; suitable after interfaces stabilize
files: `clock-windows/src/settings.rs` and app settings coordination; use existing format/store/render APIs.
before: `settings.py` is 3,463 lines and `welcome.py` 1,279; most options are intentionally outside the reduced product.
scope: Build one native dialog for format/presets, primary/all displays, point size and theme; add Apply/Cancel and explicit Reload.
Preview current time plus the documented New Year examples, clearly labeling ISO week-year versus calendar-year presets.
Use the core parser errors and renderer per-monitor fit checks. Apply persists valid config before dispatching ConfigApplied; failed save keeps old live state and dialog edits.
Cancel discards unsaved edits; duplicate launch/settings menu focuses the same dialog. Provide proper labels/tab order, keyboard actions and high-contrast behavior.
Reserve an OS-owned startup toggle interface for R12; do not invent a JSON startup flag or auto-enable startup.
accept: Entering `%g%V.%u` previews 2642.2 for the fixture and explains the New Year distinction.
Malformed tokens, oversize format, font bounds and layout overflow produce actionable messages without crashing or clipping tray icons.
Apply updates without restart; failed save/Cancel preserve old config; no wizard or per-monitor custom UI.
Dialog is keyboard/Narrator usable and works at mixed DPI.
validation: Tests for draft/apply/cancel orchestration using fake store and layout responses; interactive native controls, focus, DPI and screen-reader checks.
exclude: No settings parity port, external links/news panel, startup implementation, file watcher, HTML or custom timezone editor.
handoff: Dialog screenshots, keyboard/tab behavior and validation/save failure demonstrations.

title: Add clap diagnostics, deterministic format CLI and capped tracing logs
level: General Rust agent; Windows CLI I/O verification required
files: `clock-app/src/{cli,diagnostics,logging}.rs`, safe console wrapper in clock-windows and CLI integration tests.
before: Python stdout capture/report() and crash browser URL have no stable machine-readable diagnostic contract. scat provides clap, serde_json and tracing conventions.
scope: Implement no-subcommand GUI plus `format --format --at`, `config validate --config`, `doctor --json`, and `settings`; use clap derive.
Apply config path precedence --config > ELEVEN_CLOCK_CONFIG > LocalAppData default. Format/validate must not acquire GUI mutex or initialize Explorer.
Doctor uses bounded read-only R02 probing, schema_version 1, exact OS build/architecture, strategy, per-monitor geometry/DPI and explicit unsupported reasons; no new IPC protocol.
Keep stdout exclusively command output/JSON and diagnostics on stderr. Exit 0 success, 1 runtime/I/O, 2 invalid input/config, 3 unsupported shell.
GUI-subsystem binary must attach to parent console only for CLI mode and preserve redirected handles; test PowerShell piping. No console flash on normal launch.
Use tracing/RUST_LOG with local logs capped at 1 MiB and three retained files; log transitions rather than repaint spam. No automatic uploads.
accept: Fixture command for 2026-10-13 prints exactly 2642.2; invalid input returns 2.
PowerShell redirected JSON parses cleanly; help/format/validation work without running Explorer overlays.
Doctor returns unsupported reason/exit 3 on unavailable shell and never changes Explorer.
Rotation is bounded and logs contain no usernames/window titles/config paths by default.
validation: CLI process tests for exit codes, stdout/stderr and config precedence; Windows PowerShell redirect/pipe smoke tests; log rotation test with small injected limits.
exclude: No network diagnostics service, running-instance RPC, telemetry, crash URL upload or unrelated scat commands.
handoff: CLI help/examples, versioned JSON sample, exit-code tests and Windows redirected-output evidence.

title: Implement opt-in per-user login startup with distinct app identity
level: Small Windows integration task; suitable for a bounded agent assignment
files: `clock-windows/src/startup.rs`, the R10 startup checkbox adapter and focused tests.
before: `ElevenClock.iss:130` writes HKCU Run value `elevenClock`; copying it would conflict with the legacy app.
scope: Define a distinct ElevenClockRust startup value under HKCU Run and use an absolute correctly quoted executable path. No admin privileges.
Settings reads actual registration state and enables/disables only this app's exact value on explicit user action.
Do not store a second startup boolean in JSON. Surface failures and leave unrelated values untouched.
Handle spaces/Unicode paths and stale/moved portable executable with a diagnostic and explicit repair action; do not silently enable startup.
Document installer cooperation: uninstall removes only the Rust-owned registration.
accept: Startup defaults off and enabling/disabling affects only the dedicated Rust key.
Windows logon starts exactly one instance through the existing mutex.
Paths containing spaces/Unicode round-trip; failed write leaves checkbox consistent with OS state.
Legacy ElevenClock startup and preferences remain unchanged.
validation: Unit-test command quoting/state reconciliation; use a temporary test registry value for integration tests; explicit manual logon test and cleanup.
exclude: No scheduled task, service, machine-wide registry writes, installer implementation or silent repair of legacy startup.
handoff: Exact owned registry value/app identity, quoting tests, manual logon evidence and uninstall contract.

title: Run Windows compatibility, recovery and performance acceptance gates
level: Windows validation agent; real interactive hardware/VM access required
files: `docs/windows-evidence/acceptance.md`, repeatable measurement scripts and focused regression fixtures for observed failures.
before: Legacy Basic health check installs dependencies and runs compileall. It does not demonstrate shell behavior or resource stability.
scope: Execute the dissection's matrix on two exact stock Windows 11 x64 builds and record OS patch, app commit, CPU/logical cores, monitors, DPI and themes.

Cover one/two displays, negative origins, primary swap/hotplug, 100/125/150/200% mixed DPI, auto-hide, fullscreen per monitor, native calendar/neighbor clicks, Narrator, lock/resume and time/timezone changes.
Exercise Explorer restart, forced app kill, repeated launch/settings cycles, invalid config, overflow and unsupported discovery.

Measure ten minutes each of date-only/minute/seconds modes: CPU-time delta divided by wall time × logical processors, private working set, handles, threads, timer/discovery rate. Include any helper process.
Run eight-hour soak and report resource trends. Targets: <0.2% total CPU and <40 MiB private working set on recorded reference hardware; failures must be documented, not silently waived.
Write a pass/fail support matrix. File/fix concrete blockers through scoped follow-ups and rerun affected checks.
accept: Evidence names the exact app commit/build combinations and includes reproducible commands and captured results.
Every required compatibility case is passed or explicitly blocks release/narrows documented support.
Forced termination reveals native clock; no leaked hooks/windows or growing resource counts.
Performance/soak results are measured; no claim based only on a microbenchmark, CI run or simulation.
validation: Run actual matrix and attached measurement scripts; use R11 doctor output to tie results to configuration/build. No synthetic 'pass' fixtures.
exclude: No unreviewed scope reduction, invented screenshots, fabricated performance values or wholesale architecture changes.
handoff: Release-gate report and exact supported builds. Keep unchecked if desktop access or eight-hour execution is unavailable.

title: Package native x64 releases and verify licensing, install and rollback
level: Windows release agent; licensing conclusions must be evidence-backed
files: Rust release workflow, dedicated packaging files, notices, release/rollback docs and installer smoke-test scripts.
before: `build.cmd` bundles PyInstaller/PySide6 and strips DLLs; old Inno Setup AppId/startup/reset actions target legacy ElevenClock. README says Apache while LICENSE is GPL v3.
scope: Produce locked MSVC release executable and ZIP containing source/version provenance, applicable notices and SHA256 checksums; preserve separate debug symbols as a CI artifact.
Verify native runtime DLL requirements on a clean supported Windows machine; document if runtime installation is needed instead of claiming a self-contained EXE without testing.
Resolve README/LICENSE discrepancy by tracing applicable source/assets and preserving obligations; do not relicense merely because code is Rust. Block distribution if unresolved.

Create per-user installer with a new AppId, install directory, executable/startup identity and uninstall behavior. Portable ZIP is the first artifact; installer follows successful portable smoke tests.
Check install/update/uninstall, path quoting, startup disabled default, coexistence with legacy files and rollback to old release. Do not run both overlay apps at once during validation.
Release workflow uploads artifacts on PR/manual runs; publishing versioned releases/signing requires configured identity and release action, not automatic creation during this issue.
accept: Clean Windows portable run and installer lifecycle pass with no Python/Qt runtime.
Uninstall removes only owned files/startup registration; existing legacy config survives.
Artifacts have checksums, source commit and consistent notices; any unsigned status is accurate.
Rollback steps actually restore an earlier supported executable/native clock.
validation: Locked release build, CLI smoke tests, ZIP checksum verification and clean-VM portable/install/update/uninstall/rollback matrix; record signing availability without claiming signatures.
exclude: No auto-updater, store submission, reuse of legacy installer identity or public release announcement.
handoff: Artifact links, dependency/runtime report, licensing evidence and install/rollback results.

title: Cut over to Rust and retire legacy runtime/build workflows
level: Repository integration agent; only after release gates pass
files: Root README/contributor docs, root Cargo workspace relocation if chosen, legacy Python/build/workflow removals and migration guide.
before: The repository still defaults to the original Python/Qt app while the rewrite lives under rust/; archived code remains useful until acceptance completes.
scope: Verify R13/R14 passed for the exact candidate and record a legacy reference tag/commit before deleting working-tree files.
Make Rust the default documented build/run path and update CI/dependency-update paths consistently. If moving rust/ to root, update every manifest/script/example and rerun all checks.
Remove obsolete Python/PyInstaller/Qt runtime, old build commands and Python/translation/update workflows from active release tree; retain required licenses/notices and useful historical docs in Git.

Rewrite README for actual supported builds/features and migration limitations. Include format presets, diagnostics and rollback; do not advertise old internet sync/notification/custom-gesture features.
Preserve users' legacy config/startup choice; document disabling the old overlay before running Rust. No automatic import/destructive reset.
Open final integration PR into main with release evidence; do not auto-merge it.
accept: Fresh checkout follows Rust docs and passes required CI; active release tree does not depend on Python/Qt.
All removed features and unsupported platforms are accurately documented.
Legacy baseline remains retrievable and user data untouched.
Final PR links exact acceptance/package evidence and requires no undocumented local setup.
validation: Fresh Windows build/run, Linux core checks, full applicable CI, link/path checks and rollback instructions against the tagged baseline.
exclude: No main auto-merge, deletion of history/tags/user preferences or additional feature work.
handoff: Final integration PR, migration guide, legacy reference and verified CI/artifact links.
